faq.a: Nuaman is associated with the Arabic form نُعْمَان, whose core sense is nuaman; blood; anemone flower.

faq.q: What is the origin of Nuaman?
faq.a: Nuaman is associated with Arabic. Nuaman is Arabic نُعْمَان (Nuʿmān), a lexical item denoting blood and also a red flower (anemone).
Yes — the underlying form نُعْمَان is Arabic.
Nuaman can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Nuaman should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Nuʿmān is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.a: In Urdu, Nuaman is rendered نعمان and carries the sense نعمان، خون؛ سرخ پھول.

faq.q: What does Nuaman mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Nuaman is rendered نعمان and carries the sense نعمان، خون؛ گل سرخ.
A romanized syllable approximation is nua-man. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Nuaman?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Nuaman, nuaman. Script forms are نعمان, نُعْمَان, नुमान.

faq.q: Is Nuaman a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
